judgements.referenceQuote: He has been CEO of IBM since April 2020 and chairman since January 2021.
judgements.evidenceQuote: He has been CEO of IBM since April 2020.
judgements.rationale: The dossier states the CEO part with the same date ('He has been CEO of IBM since April 2020.') and separately states the chairman part with the same date ('He has been chairman since January 2021.', claim 8c649ac1549164616b5395ce01e7b1f5). Together the two claims state the same fact with the same subject and dates, so the compound reference fact is recovered; the quoted evidence is from the CEO-half claim.

judgements.referenceQuote: He was a driving force behind IBM's $34 billion acquisition of Red Hat, which closed in July 2019.
judgements.evidenceQuote: He was a principal architect of the acquisition of Red Hat.
judgements.rationale: The dossier states Krishna's driving role in the Red Hat acquisition ('principal architect'; also 'Krishna spearheaded many of the next-generation IBM initiatives like the Red Hat acquisition', claim feba17755e2d039aba23deaa4494749d), but it does not state the $34 billion value, the July 2019 closing date, or that the transaction was IBM's, so only part of the reference fact is recovered.

judgements.referenceQuote: Krishna joined IBM's Thomas J. Watson Research Center in 1990, and continued in Watson Research for 18 years until 2009. judgements.evidenceQuote: Krishna began his career at IBM in 1990.

overclaims.statement: Arvind Krishna is senior vice president and director, IBM Research.
overclaims.citedQuote: Arvind Krishna is senior vice president and director, IBM Research.
overclaims.rationale: The ITIF bio passage describes Krishna's pre-CEO role leading IBM Research. He has been IBM CEO since April 2020 and chairman since January 2021 (per the Wikipedia and other citations in this same dossier), so presenting this as his current position ('is senior vice president and director') states a past role as current. The dossier even marks this duplicate claim 'supported' while marking the identical claim 'contested'.

overclaims.statement: he helps guide the company’s overall technical strategy, leading a global organization of approximately 3,000 scientists and technologists located at 12 labs on six continents.
overclaims.citedQuote: he helps guide the company’s overall technical strategy, leading a global organization of approximately 3,000 scientists and technologists located at 12 labs on six continents.
overclaims.rationale: This present-tense description comes from the same outdated ITIF bio of Krishna's tenure heading IBM Research. Since he became CEO in 2020, 'he helps guide the company's overall technical strategy, leading... 3,000 scientists' no longer describes his current role, yet the dossier asserts it without dating it.

overclaims.statement: I would you, we're very practical people
overclaims.rationale: The cited 'Leadership Reimagined' podcast transcript quote is 'Stuart Levine' — the speaker is Stuart Levine, not Arvind Krishna. Attributing this first-person remark to Krishna misattributes authorship; the quote itself names the actual speaker.

overclaims.statement: we're very practical people and we compete, I have to say, pretty well with the larger brand names in consultancy
overclaims.rationale: This remark about competing with large consultancy brands fits Stuart Levine's consulting firm, the actual speaker on this podcast episode, not Krishna. The cited quote ('your firm') does not even textually support the statement, and the speaker attribution points to Levine.

overclaims.statement: I actually ended up working there for about three years
overclaims.citedQuote: I actually ended up working there for about three years
overclaims.rationale: This first-person career anecdote comes from the 'Leadership Reimagined' podcast, whose speaker is Stuart Levine, not Arvind Krishna. Krishna's documented career (IBM since 1990) is not what this remark describes.

overclaims.statement: I'm still involved at Northwell Health
overclaims.citedQuote: I'm still involved at Northwell Health
overclaims.rationale: Northwell Health involvement is Stuart Levine's affiliation (he speaks on his own leadership podcast); there is no evidence tying this to Arvind Krishna. The dossier attributes another person's first-person statement to Krishna.

overclaims.statement: You can go to your website. StuartLevine.com
overclaims.rationale: The quoted website StuartLevine.com belongs to Stuart Levine, the podcast's speaker. Presenting this as a claim about Arvind Krishna is a clear misattribution to a different person.

overclaims.statement: We publish current information called planet governance
overclaims.citedQuote: We publish current information called planet governance
overclaims.rationale: This publication ('planet governance') is described by Stuart Levine, the actual speaker of the podcast transcript cited. It is not Arvind Krishna's or IBM's publication, so the dossier attributes someone else's statement to Krishna.

overclaims.statement: Arvind Krishna was featured on TIME’s 2026 list of the 100 Most Influential People in AI.
overclaims.citedQuote: TIME’s 2026 list of the 100 Most Influential People in AI
overclaims.rationale: The cited quote mentions 'TIME's 2026 list of the 100 Most Influential People in AI' and, from the same source, 'nine Indian-origin figures working across technology', but neither passage explicitly states that Krishna himself was featured on the list. The claim asserts his inclusion beyond what the cited text supports.

overclaims.statement: Arvind Krishna is identified as an Indian-origin figure working in technology.
overclaims.citedQuote: nine Indian-origin figures working across technology
overclaims.rationale: The cited quote ('nine Indian-origin figures working across technology') refers to a group of nine figures but does not itself name Krishna as one of them; the linkage is inferred rather than stated in the cited passage.

usefulness.rationale: The dossier firmly establishes who Arvind Krishna is: IBM Chairman and CEO (since April 2020 / January 2021 as chairman), his IIT Kanpur and University of Illinois education, his 1990 start at IBM, the Red Hat acquisition, and rich recent material on his AI and quantum views (2026 CNBC, CRN, Yahoo Finance). However, a whole cluster of first-person statements from the 'Leadership Reimagined' podcast (Northwell Health, StuartLevine.com, consultancy competition) is misattributed to Krishna when the speaker is Stuart Levine, and an outdated ITIF bio is used to assert his pre-CEO IBM Research role in the present tense. These contaminate the overview/career/ideas sections. The dossier rarely states what it does not know — gaps are only implicit in 'contested'/'claimed' statuses — so a reader could still be misled in meeting prep despite the strong core.
